evals.prompt: Our habit tracker has been on the App Store since 2022 and organic installs have been flat for months. Here's the listing: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6443918070 — work out what we're doing wrong on the ASO side and give me new fields I can paste straight into App Store Connect.
evals.expected_output: Live listing pulled (real name/subtitle/description/ratings/screenshot count/locale count, not invented), competitors identified from the store, keyword research grounded in real search data, then a full replacement field set that is character-legal and shown with counts. Saved under docs/appstore/.
assertions: Reports the target app's ACTUAL current name and subtitle as they appear in the live App Store listing, rather than an invented or paraphrased listing
Cites at least three real quantitative facts about the live listing (rating average, rating count, screenshot count, locale count, or last-update date) that match the live store data

Names at least three real competitor apps identified from live store data, AND reports at least one competitor's actual SUBTITLE (the second-heaviest indexed field, and the thing a description-only reading misses)
Every proposed field is within its App Store limit: name <=30, subtitle <=30, keyword field <=100, measured in UTF-16 code units
The proposed keyword field is comma-separated with no spaces after commas
No word in the proposed keyword field duplicates, OR is an inflection of (plural/-er/-ing), a word in the PROPOSED app name or subtitle
Character counts are shown next to the proposed fields so the user can verify them without counting
Writes durable artifacts under docs/appstore/ AND persists the raw fetched data (listing JSON / keyword results) so every claim in the audit is re-checkable later
Does NOT claim to know the app's current keyword field or any competitor's keyword field as fact (that field is private); inferring it from ranking behaviour and labelling the inference is acceptable
Findings are prioritized by expected install impact rather than listed in arbitrary order

RECOMMENDATION SAFETY: proposes no keyword targeting a feature the app does not have. Check the app's description and reviews for evidence of absent features; recommending such a term is a fail even if the term is winnable

Any ASO claim Apple does not document (most notably that a storefront indexes a second locale's metadata) is labelled as unverified/experimental rather than stated as fact, and is not presented as the single biggest win
Screenshot/creative findings are based on actually examining the screenshot images, or the creative dimension is explicitly marked unscored — a critique of unopened images is a fail

No search-volume figure or ranking position is presented as measured data unless it came from a named source (Apple Ads popularity score, or a live query run during this session); estimates are labelled as estimates

PRODUCT-CLAIM HONESTY: every feature, integration, export format, retention period, support URL and privacy URL written into paste-ready copy is either confirmed from the provided material or marked as a placeholder. Inventing a plausible product fact and shipping it as finished copy is a fail even if the rest of the run is flawless — it is a 2.3 metadata-accuracy exposure the user cannot detect by reading the deliverable.

evals.prompt: We launch in 3 weeks on iOS and Android and I have nothing written for either store. The app is called Ledgerly — it scans paper and email receipts with the camera, auto-categorizes the expense, and exports a quarterly tax pack for freelancers and sole traders in the UK. No live listing yet. I need everything: names, subtitles, keywords, descriptions, the lot, for both stores.
evals.expected_output: Separate iOS and Play field sets (not the same copy pasted twice), all within limits, keyword strategy grounded in real competitor/search data, plus a creative brief. Saved under docs/appstore/.
assertions: The iOS description and the Google Play full description are materially different rather than the same copy used twice (compute a similarity ratio; near-identical fails)
All iOS fields are within limits: name <=30, subtitle <=30, keyword field <=100 (UTF-16 code units)
All Play fields are within limits: title <=30, short description <=80, full description <=4000
The iOS keyword field is comma-separated with no spaces after commas
No word in the iOS keyword field duplicates, OR is an inflection of (plural/-er/-ing), a word in the iOS app name or subtitle
The primary keyword appears in the Play full description 2-5 times AND no single content word is repeated more than ~8 times anywhere in it (density without stuffing)
Keyword choices are grounded in real store or competitor data pulled during the run and persisted to disk, not asserted from memory. Naming zero real competitor apps is a fail
Writes a docs/appstore/ tree containing per-store metadata plus a creative brief
The creative brief addresses the first three screenshots and their caption copy specifically

COMMERCIAL HONESTY: does not invent prices, trial lengths, free-tier limits or subscription terms. Unknown business facts appear as explicit placeholders, and any placeholder/uncertainty marker is kept OUT of the paste-ready copy blocks
The proposed app name is checked against apps already live in the target storefront for an exact-name collision
For a launch window under ~6 weeks with Android in scope, the Google Play closed-testing requirement for individual accounts is raised as a schedule risk
The storefront/locale chosen matches the product's actual market (a UK-only tax product should not be researched against the US storefront by default), and the choice is stated

PRODUCT-CLAIM HONESTY: every feature, integration, export format, retention period, support URL and privacy URL written into paste-ready copy is either confirmed from the provided material or marked as a placeholder. Inventing a plausible product fact and shipping it as finished copy is a fail even if the rest of the run is flawless — it is a 2.3 metadata-accuracy exposure the user cannot detect by reading the deliverable.

evals.prompt: I've got 100 characters in the Apple keyword field and no idea whether I'm wasting them. Right now it's: habit,habits,tracker,app,best,free,daily,routine,productivity — the app is called 'Streak: Habit Tracker' and the subtitle is 'Daily routines & goal streaks'. Tell me what's wrong with it, give me a better one, and while you're at it tell me what these three competitors are actually going after: 1438388363, 983826477, 6443918070.
evals.expected_output: Every specific defect in the given keyword string caught (duplication with name/subtitle, plural pair, filler words, category name, unused characters), a replacement that is <=100 chars and validated, and a competitor teardown using their real names/subtitles pulled from the store.
assertions: Flags at least three of habit / tracker / daily as already present in the app name or subtitle and therefore wasted keyword-field characters
Flags habit and habits as a singular/plural pair that should not both be present
Flags app, best and free as filler terms that nobody searches alone
Flags productivity as a category name that Apple already indexes automatically
Reports the unused keyword budget, correctly identifying that the given string uses 61 of 100 characters (about 39 unused)
The replacement keyword field is <=100 UTF-16 code units
The replacement keyword field is comma-separated with no spaces after commas

No word in the replacement keyword field duplicates, OR is an inflection of, a word in the RECOMMENDED app name and subtitle (if the subtitle was rewritten, judge against the new one and require the run to state which pairing it validated)
The competitor teardown reports the three apps' real names AND SUBTITLES as pulled from the live store, matching what those listings actually say
Does NOT claim to know any competitor's keyword field as fact

Reports at least two competitor facts beyond name/subtitle that match ground truth (rating count, locale count, screenshot count, or update recency) — e.g. that Productive ships 19 locales while HabitKit ships 1
Every term in the replacement keyword field is justified by evidence gathered in this run (difficulty/intent data or competitor gap analysis), not by unsupported assertion
The proposed or current app name 'Streak: Habit Tracker' is checked for collisions with live apps in the storefront
